_comment: Travelia Score — tunable knobs (edit + redeploy, no data re-bake). Score = 100 * Safety * Fit^wFit * Value^wValue * Reach^wReach. See docs/SCORING.md.
_sliders_doc: MIDDLE-IS-OFF: each slider is a 0..4 notch, centre (2) = off (no weight/no filter). tune() in score.ts reads the per-notch arrays below at the traveller's notch. Budget is SPEND LEVEL (not luxury): the shoestring half favours cheaper places (Value weight); the generous half just turns the price penalty off, so pricier adventures aren't down-ranked — it never implies 5-star. Travel time is gently ON at centre (wReach 0.15) so Home always tilts the map toward reachable places — the north star is value from a real home town, and the map otherwise has no distance signal (Value scores from country price, not the all-in cost). Reach decays by door-to-door HOURS (a flight-time model in score.ts). Slide toward 'far ok' (notch 3-4) to turn it fully off for global dream trips. Temp & Safety are two-sided. Profiles are named notch presets; moving any slider switches to Custom.
_fresh_doc: Mugginess is a PENALTY on comfort, not a component of it: `mug` is the share of a trip's comfort that a fully oppressive month costs. It reads the monthly mean dew point (index.arrow `dewp`, pipeline/humid_bake.py), which falls from no penalty at or below comfort.mugLo to the full one at or above mugHi — the standard dew-point comfort scale (16 °C noticeable, 18 sticky, 21 uncomfortable, 24 oppressive). Dew point rather than relative humidity because RH means nothing without a temperature and would double-count `warm`; dew point is bounded by air temperature, so the term is silent in winter by construction. A penalty rather than a sixth comfort sub-score because a weighted mean pulls both ways: as a component, dry air scored a full mark and lifted a freezing Prague January on the city map from 32 to 42 for the sole merit of not being humid. Weighted heaviest for hiking/city/culture (a full day on your feet, no water to get into), light for beach (sea breeze, swimming — and the tropics are chosen knowingly), and absent for diving (underwater) and ski (a sub-zero dew point cannot be muggy).
_tripQuality_doc: Experience trips rank by a continuous 0..1 quality column (index_quality.arrow) instead of a binary tag filter — so no place is ever wrongly invisible (Karlovy Vary on the culture map). Physical trips (beach/ski/diving) are absent here: they keep their real geo+climate gate, and take their quality (if any) from physicalQuality below — quality = 1 only where no sweep exists.
_physicalQuality_doc: Quality columns for PHYSICAL trips — applied on top of their hard geo+climate+tag gate (which stays; unlike tripQuality this never turns the gate off). beach = OSM beach/resort density (beach_quality.py), a bonus-only 0.55..1.0 floor so unmapped coasts are un-boosted, never tanked — it separates a resort coast from an iron-ore port with identical warm/dry/coastal signals. ski = OSM lift/piste density (ski_quality.py), floored LOWER at 0.45..1.0 because a chairlift is capital infrastructure mappers reliably add, so its absence is real evidence you cannot ski there — where an unmapped beach still exists. diving = OSM reef + dive-operator density (diving_quality.py), floored at 0.50 (between the two) because the evidence is mixed — a reef exists unmapped, but a dive centre is capital mappers do add — and underwater mapping is the thinnest of the three; it separates a real dive coast from any merely warm sea, which is all the 18-24 C gate tests.
_terrain_doc: A RESIDUAL nudge, no longer the main event. This was a 0.7/0.6 stopgap for a 'nature' column that knew nothing about parks, and it ramped the destination's OWN point elevation — so it rescued places that sit high while still reading every valley gateway town as flat. Measured 2026-08-24: Innsbruck/Interlaken/Berchtesgaden scored 27 against a global median of 29, and Munich outranked all three on the hiking map — the very bug this was added to fix. The proper fix it called for is now built: park_quality.py (protected-area proximity, all 234k) and relief_bake.py (highest peak within 25 km MINUS the town's elevation) are baked INTO the nature column by quality.py, where relief is measured rather than inferred from altitude. Keeping a small weight here is deliberate: high ground is mild evidence of terrain in its own right, and the residual keeps the blend alive so a future re-tune has somewhere to go. Do not raise it back — at 0.7 it double-counts relief and re-inverts valleyBase vs highPlateau in check-score.mjs.

attractions._doc: Theme parks & attractions — the WHAT, never the WHO (see attractions_quality.py: `family` is already a WHO_PAX value AND an unrelated tagbit). Gate is `temperate`, not `none` like city/culture, because queueing outdoors in 36 C with children is the entire failure mode — and it is what makes the lens useful: Orlando in April really should beat Orlando in August. rainKill is tighter than hiking's 400 since most of the estate is open-air, and mug matches hiking (a full day on your feet, no water to get into).
